items.priority_name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
items.title: Priority 1: central question
items.description: How do students move through key academic and postsecondary pathways, where do differences in access and outcomes emerge, and which student, school, and system conditions are associated with successful transitions?

items.priority_name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
items.title: Early learning pathways
items.description: What do longitudinal literacy and mathematics pathways reveal about when differences in achievement, placement, and risk first emerge?

items.priority_name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
items.title: Middle-grades transitions
items.description: What prior academic, attendance, intervention, placement, and school-context factors predict Grade 8 mathematics placement and success?

items.priority_name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
items.title: Advanced learning access
items.description: Who participates in advanced learning opportunities, including AIG, honors, AP/IB, advanced mathematics, CCP, advanced CTE, CDM, and related pathways, and where are the largest opportunity gaps?

items.priority_name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
items.title: Postsecondary pathways
items.description: How do students transition from high school into postsecondary education, credentials, and other outcomes, and which K–12 experiences are associated with successful transitions?

items.priority_name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
items.title: School-sector pathways
items.description: How do enrollment, mobility, access, and outcomes vary across school contexts, including charter schools and for populations such as Students with Disabilities?

items.priority_name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
items.title: Priority 2: central question
items.description: How do workforce supply, qualifications, working conditions, staffing models, and professional supports affect educator and student-support workforce stability, service capacity, and student outcomes?

items.priority_name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
items.title: Supply and stability
items.description: Where are vacancies, attrition, mobility, and staffing shortages concentrated across educators, school leaders, and specialized instructional support personnel, and which working conditions best predict subsequent workforce instability across educator experience levels and school contexts?

items.priority_name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
items.title: Working conditions
items.description: How do school leadership, planning time and workload, educator voice, safety, professional learning, and instructional support relate to staff well-being, retention, and effectiveness; are there recurring combinations of conditions or thresholds associated with elevated risk?

items.priority_name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
items.title: Qualifications and staffing
items.description: How are licensure, certification, staffing ratios, caseloads, and other workforce characteristics associated with student and organizational outcomes?

items.priority_name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
items.title: Professional learning and leadership
items.description: Which professional learning, coaching, leadership, and role-design approaches improve educator practice and support, and how do leadership, time, safety, and professional learning interact to influence workforce outcomes?

items.priority_name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
items.title: Bright spots
items.description: Which schools and districts achieve stronger workforce stability or teacher working conditions than expected given their context, or show sustained improvement across survey administrations, and what organizational practices distinguish them?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: Priority 3: central question
items.description: Which programs, policies, and practices improve student or educator outcomes, for whom, under what conditions, and at what cost?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: Effectiveness
items.description: What effects are associated with major state, local, and federally funded (e.g., Title I-IX) initiatives, policies, programs, and activities, including their effects on educator working conditions, retention, and student outcomes?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: Implementation
items.description: How do implementation, dosage, fidelity, staffing, leadership, educator workload, and local context influence effectiveness?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: Variation in effects
items.description: Which students, schools, districts, or communities benefit most or least, and why?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: Cost and return on investment
items.description: What are the costs associated with different approaches relative to their outcomes, and when do benefits justify costs?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: Scalability and transferability
items.description: Which promising approaches can be implemented successfully across different North Carolina contexts?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: New initiatives and pilots
items.description: How effectively are newly funded programs, staffing or organizational redesigns, and instructional innovations implemented, and which improve working conditions, educator stability, or student outcomes?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: Emerging instructional approaches and technologies
items.description: How do new instructional models, educational technologies, and AI-enabled tools affect teaching practices, student learning, educator workload, and operational efficiency?

items.priority_name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
items.title: Continuation and expansion decisions
items.description: Which investments demonstrate sufficient effectiveness, feasibility, and cost-effectiveness to warrant continuation, modification, expansion, or discontinuation?

items.priority_name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
items.title: Priority 4: central question
items.description: How do school climate, safety, health and behavioral health supports, family engagement, and organizational conditions interact to influence attendance, behavior, well-being, and academic outcomes?

items.priority_name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
items.title: Attendance
items.description: What student, family, school, health, and community factors are most strongly associated with chronic absenteeism and attendance recovery?

items.priority_name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
items.title: Safety and discipline
items.description: How do school safety conditions, student conduct, educator perceptions of safety, and disciplinary practices relate to staff well-being and stability, student behavior, and academic outcomes?

items.priority_name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
items.title: Health and student supports
items.description: How do access to counselors, social workers, psychologists, nurses, behavioral health services, and community supports relate to attendance, discipline, crisis events, and academic outcomes?

items.priority_name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
items.title: School climate
items.description: How are staff and student perceptions of leadership, safety, belonging, support, and climate associated with teacher retention, student attendance, academic growth, and differences in outcomes across student groups?

items.priority_name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
items.title: Family engagement
items.description: Which family engagement approaches are most effective in North Carolina contexts, including rural communities and engagement of fathers and other caregivers?

items.priority_name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
items.title: Resilience and recovery
items.description: Which school, district, workforce, and community conditions support stronger recovery following major disruptions?

items.priority_name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
items.title: Priority 5: central question
items.description: How can assessment and accountability information be designed, interpreted, and used to support valid instructional, intervention, and school-improvement decisions?

items.priority_name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
items.title: Assessment selection and use
items.description: What are the relative strengths, limitations, feasibility, and instructional implications of different assessment and screening approaches?

items.priority_name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
items.title: Longitudinal interpretation
items.description: How can assessment information be used to identify meaningful learning trajectories, emerging risk, and changes in student performance over time?

items.priority_name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
items.title: Interim assessment
items.description: Where can NC Check-Ins and other interim measures support valid targeting, cohort monitoring, and instructional decisions, and where should interpretation be limited?

items.priority_name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
items.title: Instructional use
items.description: How are schools and districts translating screening, benchmark, EOG, EOC, and other assessment information into instructional and intervention decisions, and which routines support effective use?

items.priority_name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
items.title: Accountability reporting
items.description: How should assessment, accountability, and school climate or workforce indicators, including Teacher Working Conditions (TWC) results, be reported so meaningful differences, trends, and school profiles remain visible and useful?

items.priority_name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
items.title: Accountability validity
items.description: How well do specific accountability measures, school benchmarks, and workforce survey constructs or composite indices predict subsequent outcomes, remain stable over time, and perform across school and district contexts?

items.priority_name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
items.title: Priority 6: central question
items.description: How do policies governing educational resources, student access, workforce flexibility, and school operations influence educational opportunities, organizational capacity, and student outcomes, and what are the potential consequences of alternative policy approaches?

items.priority_name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
items.title: Resource allocation and school finance
items.description: How do alternative funding formulas, allotment structures, and resource allocation policies affect the distribution, adequacy, flexibility, and use of educational resources across schools and districts?

items.priority_name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
items.title: Student access and opportunity
items.description: How do enrollment, assignment, eligibility, and participation policies influence access to educational opportunities, and what are their consequences for student pathways and outcomes?

items.priority_name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
items.title: Workforce and organizational flexibility
items.description: How do policies governing educator qualifications, staffing, planning time, leadership roles, educator voice, and operational authority influence working conditions, recruitment, retention, instructional capacity, and school effectiveness?

items.priority_name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
items.title: Policy implementation and administrative burden
items.description: How do state and local requirements, educator workload, administrative structures, and operational constraints influence policy feasibility, consistency, costs, and effectiveness?

items.priority_name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
items.title: Distributional effects and policy tradeoffs
items.description: How would proposed policy changes affect different students, schools, districts, and communities, and what tradeoffs arise among competing policy objectives?

items.priority_name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
items.title: Policy monitoring and evaluation
items.description: How can longitudinal data, comparative analyses, and appropriate evaluation designs inform decisions about maintaining, modifying, expanding, or discontinuing policies?

items.title: Equity and access
items.description: Who has access, who benefits, and where are disparities concentrated?

items.title: Longitudinal change
items.description: How do patterns and outcomes evolve over time?

items.title: Context
items.description: How do findings vary by geography, grade span, school size, student population, and district characteristics?

items.title: Implementation
items.description: How do dosage, fidelity, leadership, staffing, and local conditions influence results?

items.title: Consistent Data Definitions
items.description: Establish consistent definitions and coding for key measures such as economic disadvantage, vacancies, participation, services, staffing ratios, and implementation.

items.title: Shared Measures Across Offices
items.description: Identify a common set of measures that can be reused across offices and initiatives.

items.title: Measure Validation and Comparability
items.description: Develop and validate measures or composite indices, including Teacher Working Conditions survey constructs and school-level profiles, where they improve interpretation and decision-making; assess construct comparability, participation, and nonresponse across administrations.

items.title: Program Participation Indicators
items.description: Create stable participation indicators for advanced coursework, CCP, programs, and services.

items.title: Longitudinal Workforce Data
items.description: Improve longitudinal workforce files for teachers, school leaders, and specialized instructional support personnel, including privacy-protective school- or district-level links to Teacher Working Conditions results and subsequent outcomes.

items.title: Authoritative Data Sources and Updates
items.description: Establish authoritative-source and refresh rules for AP, ACT, licensure, payroll, and related data.

items.title: Cross-System Data Linkages
items.description: Improve linkages needed for postsecondary, workforce, health, and program evaluation.

items.title: Standardized Statewide Collections
items.description: Standardize Infinite Campus forms and other statewide collections where possible.

items.title: Streamlined Data Submission
items.description: Replace duplicative entry with pre-populated extracts, automated uploads, validation rules, and reusable data elements.

items.title: Implementation and Fidelity Measures
items.description: Identify the minimum information needed to document program implementation and fidelity without increasing reporting burden.

items.title: Modernized Reporting
items.description: Modernize recurring legislative, State Board, and public reporting.

items.title: Reusable Reporting Pipelines
items.description: Develop reusable reporting pipelines with traceable figures and consistent definitions.

items.title: Dashboards and Decision Support
items.description: Determine which dashboards, peer comparisons, longitudinal trends, subgroup analyses, and contextual profiles, including TWC results, are most useful to districts and external stakeholders without obscuring uncertainty or risking respondent identification.

items.title: Automated Routine Analysis
items.description: Automate routine analysis where possible so staff capacity can shift from data assembly toward interpretation and evaluation.

items.title: Instructional innovations and technology
items.description: AI-enabled academic supports, digital curricula, instructional software, and mathematics professional development (primarily Priorities 3 and 5).

items.title: Academic and student supports
items.description: Extended learning, integrated student supports, attendance early interventions, and school safety or health pilots (primarily Priorities 3 and 4).

items.title: Educator workforce development
items.description: Apprenticeships, principal preparation and recruitment supports, and alternative staffing initiatives (primarily Priorities 2 and 3).

items.title: Student pathways
items.description: CTE modernization, innovative high school models, advanced learning access, and career development planning (primarily Priorities 1 and 3).

items.title: Early learning and literacy
items.description: New screening approaches, literacy interventions, and kindergarten readiness supports (primarily Priorities 1, 3, and 5).

items.title: School finance and resource distribution
items.description: Weighted-student funding, allotment flexibility, and supplemental funding formulas (primarily Priority 6).

items.title: Enrollment and access
items.description: Open enrollment, assignment, advanced-course placement, and educational choice policies (primarily Priorities 1 and 6).

items.title: Workforce rules and school operations
items.description: Licensure flexibility, staffing policies, and innovative school governance models (primarily Priorities 2 and 6).

items.title: Accountability and decision systems
items.description: Measures, reporting requirements, and decision rules that influence the interpretation and use of school performance information (primarily Priorities 5 and 6).

items.title: Student support and access policies
items.description: School meal access, transportation, and other policies shaping participation in educational opportunities (primarily Priorities 1, 4, and 6).

items.title: Legislatively mandated studies and evaluations should be tracked separately from discretionary NCDPI research opportunities, with assigned responsibilities, deadlines, and reporting expectations recorded when applicable.
items.description: Policy-responsive planning and portfolio coordination.

items.title: When considering additional research, assess alignment with strategic priorities; likely value for policy and practice; available evidence and unanswered questions; data availability and methodological feasibility; staff and partner capacity; and the need for timely findings. Favor designs appropriate to the decision, including descriptive and longitudinal analyses, implementation research, impact evaluations, cost-effectiveness studies, and prospective policy modeling.
items.description: Policy-responsive planning and portfolio coordination.

items.title: Maintain a companion, periodically updated opportunity inventory recording each policy or initiative, its aligned research priority, proposed research question, intended decision use, potential partners, data feasibility, and relevant timing. This inventory is a planning tool and should not be treated as an approved evaluation portfolio.
items.description: Policy-responsive planning and portfolio coordination.
